To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein phosphatase activity of the PrpC protein in B. subtilis is involved in controlling the phosphorylation state and thus the activity of the Hpr protein of the phosphoenolpyruvate:sugar phosphotransfer system.

in addition to its phosphorylase activity, the HPr kinase of B. subtilis also possesses phosphatase activity and that the serine/threonyl protein phosphatase of B. subilitis, PrpC, uses HPr(S-P) as a substrate.
the protein phosphatase of the PrpC family, PrpC, is a new player in controlling the HPr phosphorylation status and thus the activity of the PTS and the expression of catabolite genes in B. subtilis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the phosphorylation state and thus the activity of the Hpr protein of the phosphoenolpyruvate:sugar phosphotransferas system.
the control of the HPr phosphorylation level in B. subtilis.
the regulation of the phosphorylation state and activity of the HPR protein of the phosphoenolpyruvate: carbohydrate phosphotransferasesystem in Bacillus subtitilis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PrpC phosphatase dephosphorylates HPr(Ser-46) in vivo, thereby counteracting the HPr kinase activity.
in B. subtilis, HPr(S-P) is phosphorylated by HPr kinase and dephosphorylated by PrpC, whereas HPr(H-P) is phosphoryated by Enzyme I and dephosphorated by the HPr kinase.
the PrpC phosphatase is the main dephosphorylating enzyme of HPr(SerP).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PrpC is involved in the deactivation of HPr(Ser-46-P) and that the HPr phosphorylation status is controlled in a balanced way by the kinase/phosphory-lase and PrpC.
PrpC is a bifunctional enzyme, which can act as a protein phosphatase and as a phosphorylase.
the HPr kinase is responsible for the phosphorylation of the Ser-46 site in HPr, whereas the HPr phosphorylase is responsible for its dephosphorylated state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PrpC is the major dephosphorylating enzyme of HPr(Ser-46-P) in B. subtilis, and thus the main regulator of the CcpA activity in this organism.

PrpC, which is known to be a key enzyme in controlling the phosphorylation state and thus the activity of the response regulator Spo0F in the sporulation pathway, is also a key enzyme in the control of the phosphorylation state, and thus the activity, of the response regulator CcpA in the PTS-dependent catabolite control pathway.
the PrpC phosphatase activity on HPr(Ser) is a significant factor in controlling the HPr phosphorylation level in vivo.
